info.title: ServiceChannel API - v.3
info.description:
The ServiceChannel API is a RESTful and stateless API. It accepts standard HTTP verbs and supports OAuth 2.0 for authorizing requests. Our API returns common HTTP status codes as well as JSON encapsulated data. See [API Overview](/basics/introduction/overview/) for the intro to ServiceChannel API.

Authentication and Authorization

You should have a ServiceChannel account, register your application, and obtain `access_token` to integrate with our API. See [Authentication and Authorization](/basics/general/authentication/) for more information. To use this API playground, click **Authorize** and sign in to ServiceChannel.

Environment

All calls in this API Reference point to the **SB2 environment**. See [Environments](/basics/general/environments/) for more information.

API Version

The current stable version of the ServiceChannel API is `v3`. In the request URL, `v3` is a version prefix that should be present. When you omit the version prefix, calls point to the minimum supported version of the API. We recommend you to always specify the API version to avoid possible errors.

post.description:
Modifies the existing business hours for the specified location.
Send this request [GET /locations/{locationId}/businesshours](/swagger/ui/index?version=3#/AfterHours/GETv3_locations__locationId__businesshours) to get the location business hours.
Learn [how to manage business hours](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/683409418/Managing+Business+Hours+and+Holidays+for+a+Location) in ServiceChannel University.
**Example Request** POST / locations/{locationId}/businesshours { "businessHours": [ { "DayOfWeek": "Monday", "OpenTime": "10:15 AM", "CloseTime": "06:00 PM", "ClosedAllDay": false } }

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the subscriber’s location you want to change business hours for.

parameters.name: businessHoursModel
parameters.description: Request model to update business hours.

200.description: Business hours are updated for the specified location.

The request is not accepted due to bad syntax, missing parameters, insufficient data, etc.
Error codes:
613 — Incorrect format of the Open Time or Close Time. Valid format: HH:mm or hh:mm tt (for example, 23:59 or 11:59 PM).
614 — Business Hours should not overlap between days of the week
615 — Incorrect format of the day of the week. Valid values: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
616 — Duplicate 'Day of the Week' value;
617 — Business Hours are not set for the location. For the initial setup, configure Business Hours for each day of the week.
618 — Open Time or Close Time cannot be empty for a specific day of the week
628 — Incorrect format of the `Close All Day` value. Valid values: true, false.

Adds a holiday to the specified location.
Send this request [GET /locations/{locationId}/holidays](/swagger/ui/index?version=3#/AfterHours/GETv3_locations__locationId__holidays) to get the location holidays.
Learn [how to manage holidays for a location](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/683409418/Managing+Business+Hours+and+Holidays+for+a+Location) in ServiceChannel University.
**Example Request** POST /locations/{locationId}/holidays { "HolidayName": "Happy Weekend", "OpenTime": "10:00 AM", "CloseTime": "06:00 PM", "ClosedAllDay": false, "Frequency": "Yearly", "StartDate": "2021-07-03T00:10:00.308Z", "RepeatEvery": "1", "RepeatBy": "DayOfWeek", "RepeatOnDays": [ "Saturday", "Sunday" ], "RepeatOnMonths": [ “June”, "July", "August" ] }

The request is not accepted due to bad syntax, missing parameters, insufficient data, etc.

616 — Duplicate 'Day of the Week' value
619 — Incorrect format of the `Repeat by status` value. Valid values: DayOfWeek, DayOfMonth.
620 — List of days cannot be empty when submitting the `Weekly` frequency
621 — List of months cannot be empty when submitting the `Yearly` frequency
622 — Incorrect month format. Valid values: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.
623 — The `Holiday Name` value cannot be empty. The maximum length is 100 characters.
624 — Incorrect format of the 'Repeat every' value. The value should be a number between 1 and 60.
625 — The same month is specified twice in the 'Month' value
626 — Incorrect format of the frequency. Valid values: Weekly, Monthly, Yearly, Singular.
627 — Start date cannot be an empty value
628 — Incorrect format of the `Close All Day` value. Valid values: true, false.
3502 — The holiday name is already in use. Please suggest another name.

post.description: Creates a new asset type meter for a particular asset type for the current subscriber.

parameters.name: request
parameters.description:
Request to add an asset type meter.
Pass the following parameters in the request:
 • **Id** (*Required*). Enter 0 or null so that when the asset type meter is created the system can assign a unique numeric ID to it.
 • **Name** (*Required*). Name of an asset type meter.
 • **Notes**. Comments provided by a user who added the asset type meter.
 • **Inactive**. Set the asset type meter to the active on inactive status. Valid values: *true*, *false* or 1 - true, 0 - false.
 • **EditOnWO**. Define whether technicians are allowed to enter data on work orders for the asset. Valid values: *true*, *false* or 1 - true, 0 - false.
 • **AssetTypeId** (*Required*). ID of an asset type to assign the meter to.
 • **UnitOfMeasure** (*Required*). Unique numeric identifier of a unit of measurement in the system.

[Returns standard checklists](/guides/checklists/find-and-filter-checklists/) along with their parameters, configured questions, and answer options.
You can filter checklists by:  • **Trade**. Specify either `tradeid` or `tradeName`.  • **Category**. Enter either `categoryid` or `categoryName`.  • **Location**. put.description:
Updates the status of the specified proposal to *Rejected*.
You can send a proposal rejection notification to a specific user or to all users from the **Proposals/Proposal Alerts** list.  • `ProviderEmail` and `UserEmail`. Use these parameters to send a proposal rejection notification to a specific user. If passed, any of these parameters prevails over `useProposalAlertEmails`. In case you pass a value to the `ProviderEmail` or `UserEmail` parameter in the request body and set `useProposalAlertEmails` to `true`, a notification is sent to the specified email address, while users from the **Proposals/Proposal Alerts** list are not notified.  • `useProposalAlertEmails`. Set this parameter to `true` to send proposal rejection notifications to all users listed in the **Proposals/Proposal Alerts** section of **Dispatch Preferences**.

**Example Request** PUT /proposals/{proposalId}/reject { "Comments": "The project is canceled", "ProviderEmail": "", "UserEmail": "", "RejectReasonCodeId": 7, "ActionSource": "Standard", "ReasonString": "", "PinNote": false, }

put.summary: Update the specified work activity of a work order
put.description:
Updates the specified work activity of a work order by setting the check-in and check-out date and time values passed in the request.
Before updating a work activity, please consider the following:  • You can update work activities only for work orders in the *In Progress* primary status.  • The check-in date and time cannot be greater than the check-out date and time.  • The check-in date and time cannot be earlier than the scheduled date and time of the work order.  • The time range of the work activity you are updating cannot overlap the time ranges of existing work activities of the work order.  • The name will be set to the API caller name if the `name` value is not provided.
***Note:*** Both subscribers and providers can use this method.
***Note:*** Only users with extended permissions can update the work activities created by other users along with updating the `name` parameter. The users with certain permissions are:  • Subscribers that have the *Admin* role. These users can update the work activities created both by subscribers and by providers.  • Providers that have the *Admin* role (with the *EditLaborItemsOnWoDetailsProvider* feature flag turned on). These users can update the work activities created by providers only.  • Providers that have the *Business Owner / Management* role (with the *EditLaborItemsOnWoDetailsProvider* feature flag turned on). These users can update the work activities created by providers only.
Learn more about [updating a work activity](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/576258285/Updating+Service+Provider+Check-In+Out+Information) in ServiceChannel University.
**Example Request** PUT /workorders/{workorderId}/workactivities/{workactivityId} { "CheckInDate": "2020-11-19T11:10:36.868Z", "CheckOutDate": "2020-11-19T12:30:36.868Z", "Name": "John Doe" }

parameters.description: The unique numeric identifier of the work order for which you want to update a work activity.

parameters.name: workactivityId
parameters.description: The unique numeric identifier of the work activity to update.

parameters.description: Request to update a work activity.

post.summary: Create a work activity for the specified work order
post.description:
Creates a new work activity for the specified work order. The work activity type can be either *Travel* or *Repair*. Note that custom types may be configured for a subscriber.
Before creating a work activity, please consider the following:  • You can create work activities only for work orders in the *In Progress* primary status.  • The check-in date and time cannot be greater than the check-out date and time.  • The check-in date and time cannot be earlier than the scheduled date and time of the work order.  • The time range of the work activity you are creating cannot overlap the time ranges of existing work activities of the work order.  • The name will be set to the API caller name if the `name` value is not provided.
***Note:*** Both subscribers and providers can use this method.
***Note:*** Only users with extended permissions can specify the technician's name while creating a work activity. The users with extended permissions are:  • Subscribers that have the *Admin* role.  • Providers that have the *Admin* role (with the *EditLaborItemsOnWoDetailsProvider* feature flag turned on).  • Providers that have the *Business Owner / Management* role (with the *EditLaborItemsOnWoDetailsProvider* feature flag turned on).
Learn more about [creating a work activity](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/576258285/Updating+Service+Provider+Check-In+Out+Information) in ServiceChannel University.
**Example Request** POST /workorders/{workorderId}/workactivities { "WorkTypeId": "1", "CheckInDate": "2020-11-19T11:10:36.868Z", "CheckOutDate": "2020-11-19T12:15:36.868Z", "Name": "John Doe" }

get.summary: Retrieve the leak detection result on a work order

Returns the information about the leak detected on the specified work order. This answer is saved when the user answers the question “Did you find a leak?” while entering a leak inspection on a refrigerated work order.
***Note***: The *RTMultiLeakFlow* feature flag should be enabled.
The possible values in the response are the following:  • `true`: The user detected a refrigerant leak and set the answer to "Yes".  • `false`: The user didn’t detect any refrigerant leak and set the answer to "No".  • `null`: There is no information about the detected leak. get.summary: Get analytics on a work order

Retrieves analytics on the specified work order.
Analytics are based on the following flags:  • **IVR**. Tracks the proper Check-In/Out process and indicates whether the work order has both Check-In and Check-Out records and completes with a Check-Out.  • **SLA**. Tracks estimated time of arrival (ETA) and indicates whether the work order met the original ETA.  • **FirstTimeCompletionFlag**. Indicates whether the work order was completed on the first visit (the work order has only one Check-In and one Check-Out records within 24 hours).
***Note***: You can get analytics from any work order. However, the analytics are mostly relevant for the work orders in the **Completed** status, as these flags rest on the Check-In/Out information.

AssetTagStatus.description:
Validation status of the scanned asset tag. Possible values:
             • `0`=`Unknown`: Validation status is not determined.
             • `1`=`NotAvailable`: Asset tag does not exist or cannot be scanned.
             • `2`=`NotValidated`: Asset tag exists, but validation failed.
             • `3`=`PendingValidation`: Asset tag has been scanned and is awaiting validation.
             • `4`=`Validated`: Asset tag has been successfully validated.

ManuallyEntered.description: Indicates whether the asset tag value was entered manually instead of being scanned. Possible values: `true` and `false`.

AssetTagNotScannedReason.description: Free‑text explanation of why the tag was not scanned. Must not exceed 50 characters.

ValidationRequired.description: Indicates whether this asset requires asset tag validation. Possible values: `true` and `false`. To check whether validation is required, run the [GET/assets/{trackingNumber}/IsValidationRequired](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/Assets/GETv3_assets_%7BtrackingNumber%7D_IsValidationRequired) method.

AssetValidated.description: Indicates whether the asset has been successfully validated. Possible values: `true` and `false`.

UnableToValidateReasonId.description:
Standardized reason code defining why validation could not be completed. Possible values:
             • `1`: Cannot find the asset in the database
             • `2`: Cannot find the asset on site 
             • `3`: New asset
             • `4`: Other (requires explanation in `OtherReason`)
            To check the reasons and their IDs, run the [GET/assets/UnableToValidateReasons](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/Assets/GETv3_assets_UnableToValidateReasons) method.

OtherReason.description: Free-text explanation of why validation failed. Required when `UnableToValidateReasonId` = `4` (Other).

UnableToScanReasonId.description:
Standardized reason code defining why scanning could not be completed. Possible values:
             • `1`: Tag Missing
             • `2`: Tag Damaged
             • `3`: Scanner Problem
             • `4`: Other
            To get the reason codes, run the [GET/assets/UnableToScanReasons](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/Assets/GETv3_assets_UnableToScanReasons%3FsubscriberId%3D%7BsubscriberId%7D) method.

Visibility status of the attachment. Defines which parties can view the attachment. The *PrivateProviderNotesAndAttachments* feature should be enabled. For subscribers who are using Universal Connector, the *PrivateClientNotesAndAttachments* feature should be enabled.
Possible values:  • `0`: No restrictions on visibility. Visible to everyone.  • `1`: Not visible to the client. The subscriber deselected the “Visible to Client” checkmark when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.  • `2`: Not visible to the provider. The subscriber deselected the “Visible to Provider” checkmark when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.  • `3`: Visible to the subscriber only. The subscriber deselected the “Visible to Client” and “Visible to Provider” checkmarks when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.

IsInvoiceDigitalCopy.description:
Defines if the attachment is a digital copy of the provider’s invoice. According to subscriber configurations, some providers should attach digital copies of invoices. Possible values:  • `true`: The attachment is an invoice digital copy.  • `false`: The attachment is not an invoice digital copy.
***Note:*** Subscribers can set the requirement of a digital invoice copy from providers when the *InvoiceRequireDigitalCopy* feature is turned on.

Email address(es) of people who should receive an email notification about the new note. Separate multiple addresses with a semicolon.
To prevent sending email alerts, leave it empty.

ActionRequired.description: Defines whether the note should be marked with the **Action Required** flag. Possible values: `true` and `false`.

ScheduledDate.description:
Scheduled date of the work order. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`.
To change the scheduled date of the work order via this method, ensure you have the *ChangeScheduledDateViaAddNoteApiMethod* feature turned on as well as the following permission enabled: *WorkOrderScheduledDateChange*.
Without this feature and permission, the updated scheduled date will be reflected on the note but won’t automatically update the scheduled date on the work order.
To prevent updating the scheduled date, leave the `ScheduledDate` empty.

FollowUpDate.description:
To mark a note with the **Follow Up** flag, specify the follow-up date and time. It is used to revisit a work order at a later time, for example, to ensure the provider clocked in or updated the work order by the specified date. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`. Additionally, set the `IsFollowUpDateChanged` parameter to `true` if you specify the follow-up date.
When no follow-up is required, leave it empty.

IsFollowUpDateChanged.description:
Indicates whether the follow-up date should be changed. Possible input values:
             • Enter `true` if you specify the `FollowUpDate`.
             • Enter `false` if you don't specify the `FollowUpDate`.

AttachmentsIds.description: Attachment IDs that should be associated with the note. Only files already linked to the work order can be attached to the note. To get attachment IDs, run the following method: GET/odata/workorders({workorderId})/attachments.

Visibility.description:
Defines which parties can view the note. Visibility also works in Universal Connector, where there are three primary parties: *Subscriber*, *External Subscriber*, and *Provider*. Possible input values:  • `0`: Visible to everyone (subscriber, external subscriber, provider).  • `1`: Visible to the subscriber and the provider. Not visible to the external subscriber.  • `2`: Visible to the subscriber and the external subscriber. Not visible to the provider.  • `3`: Visible to the subscriber only.
Available with the *PrivateProviderNotesAndAttachments* feature flag. For Universal Connector clients, the *PrivateClientNotesAndAttachments* feature should be turned on.

Actor.description: Defines who is adding a note.

NotifyFollowers.description:
Defines whether the WO followers should be notified about the new note. Possible values:
             • `true`: WO followers will be notified.
             • `false`: WO followers will not be notified.

DoNotSendEmail.description: A flag indicating whether to suppress sending email notifications for the note. Possible input values: `true` and `false`.

IsPinned.description:
Indicates if the note should be pinned and displayed at the top of the notes list. Only one note can be pinned to a single work order.  • `true`: The note will be pinned.  • `false`: The note shouldn’t be pinned.
Available to subscribers only — behind the *PinnedNotes* feature flag.

ServiceChannel.Services.WebApi.Models.Re.description: Represents the response details of a note attachment.

Id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the attachment.

TimeStamp.description: Date and time when the attachment was added to the work order or was modified. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ss`.

NoteId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the note associated with the attachment.

Visibility.description:
Visibility status of the attachment. Defines which parties can view the attachment. The *PrivateProviderNotesAndAttachments* feature should be enabled. For subscribers who are using Universal Connector, the *PrivateClientNotesAndAttachments* feature should be enabled.
            Possible values:
             • `0`: No restrictions on visibility. Visible to everyone.
             • `1`: Not visible to the client. The subscriber deselected the **Visible to Client** checkmark when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.
             • `2`: Not visible to the provider. The subscriber deselected the **Visible to Provider** checkmark when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.
             • `3`: Visible to the subscriber only. The subscriber deselected the **Visible to Client** and **Visible to Provider** checkmarks when uploading an attachment or adding a note with an attachment.

IsInvoiceDigitalCopy.description:
Indicates whether the attachment is a digital copy of an invoice. Possible response values: `true` and `false`.
Available with the *InvoiceRequireDigitalCopy* feature flag.

ResolvedDate.description: Date and time when the action was resolved. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ssssss`.

Unique numeric identifier of the refrigerant use reason code.

Order.description: Order of appearance of a reason code.

Purpose.description:
Unique numeric identifier of the reason code for the refrigerant part use. Possible values: `0` - Leak, `1` - InitialCharge, `2` - SystemExpansion, `3` - Removal, `4` - Other, `5` - RemovedReused, `6` - Retrofit.
Each reason code on the subscriber side is associated with a hardcoded purpose value in the database. Since reason codes can vary across subscribers, the purpose helps identify the valid reason code.
***Note:*** Purpose value `0` is assigned to the `Leak` and `Repair` reason codes, indicating that a leak record gets calculated for these reason codes.

Name.description:
Reason code name for the refrigerant part use as configured by the subscriber. Possible values:
             • `Leak`
             • `Repair`
             • `Adjustment`
             • `System Expansion`
             • `Removal`
             • `Initial Charge`
             • `Retrofit`
             • `Removed Reused`

SubscriberId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the subscriber.

IsActive.description:
Defines whether a user can select a reason code when capturing refrigerant use. Possible response values:
             • `true`: Reason code is enabled.
             • `false`: Reason code is disabled.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Refrig.description: Object for adding part use records in bulk

AssetId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the asset to which the new part use records should be added. Only one asset can be processed in the request. For a non-refrigerant part use, the `AssetId` is not required.

RecId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the work order associated with the `AssetId`. Only one work order can be processed in the request.

IsRefrigerant.description: Specifies whether the part you are trying to add is classified as a refrigerant. Possible input values: `true` and `false`.

IsInventoryPart.description:
Specifies whether the part you are trying to add is listed in the inventory catalog for the location or the part is supplied by the vendor. Possible input values:
             • `true`: Indicates an inventory part
             • `false`: Indicates a vendor-supplied part

UseDate.description: Date and time when the part was used. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`.

UseDateStr.description: Date and time when the part was used. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`.

ReasonCode.description:
Reason code name for the refrigerant part use — as configured by the subscriber. Possible values:  • `Leak`  • `Repair`  • `Adjustment`  • `System Expansion`  • `Removal`  • `Initial Charge`  • `Retrofit`  • `Removed Reused`
To get the list of reason codes for the subscriber, use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/{subscriberId}/GetRefrigerantUseReasonCodes](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_%7BsubscriberId%7D_GetRefrigerantUseReasonCodes) method.

ReasonCodeId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the refrigerant use reason code. To get the list of reason code IDs for the subscriber, use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/{subscriberId}/GetRefrigerantUseReasonCodes](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_%7BsubscriberId%7D_GetRefrigerantUseReasonCodes) method.

PartGroup.description: Part group. Required only if the `IsRefrigerant` is set to `true`.

PartGroupId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the part group. Required only if the `IsRefrigerant` is set to `true`.

SupplierName.description: Name of a company that supplies the part.

Description.description: Part description. Any additional information on the part. Shouldn’t exceed 250 characters.

RefrigerantChargeOptionsId.description:
Unique numeric identifier of the charge method used. Possible values:  • `1`: Calculation  • `2`: Established  • `3`: Manufacturer Tag  • `4`: Measurement  • `5`: MFG Info (Established Range)  • `6`: Onsite Documentation  • `7`: Approximate
To get charge options and their IDs, use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/ChargeDescriptions](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_ChargeDescriptions) method.

RefrigerantChargeVendor.description: Provider who identified the initial charge of the system. Only applicable when the `ReasonCode` is set to `Initial Charge`.

InventoryLocationId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the inventory location where the inventory part is stored.

InventoryPartId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the inventory part. To get the inventory part ID, use the [GET/Setup/parts](https://inventoryapi.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html) method.

RefrigerantRemovalStatus.description:
Status that describes what was done with the removed refrigerant in the event of the retrofit plan:  • `Destroyed`  • `Reused`  • `Reclaimed`  • `Banked`  • `ChargeLost`  • `Sold`
***Note:*** Applicable for the retrofit plan.
Not recommended for use in this request.

RefrigerantTypeId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the refrigerant type. To get the list of refrigerant types and their IDs, run the [GET/refrigeranttracking/RefrigerantTypes](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_RefrigerantTypes%3FsubscriberId%3D%7BsubscriberId%7D) method.

SubmitMoeQtyExceeded.description: For Canadian locations. When the part use meets or exceeds the threshold, set the parameter’s value to `true` to be able to proceed with the request.

MoeNumber.description:
Agency number that will be assigned to the work order and the leak record. The number can be up to 20 characters. An agency number needs to be entered when the system threshold has been met or exceeded. For Canadian locations only.
Available with the *SCP_RTCanadaRefrigeration* feature flag.

IsRetrofit.description:
Specifies whether the part use is associated with a retrofit plan. Possible values:  • `true`: The part is linked to a retrofit plan. The `RefrigerantRemovalStatus` should be specified.  • `false`: The part isn’t associated with a retrofit plan.
Not recommended for use in this request.

UpdatedDate.description: Date when the open leak notification settings were last updated by the subscriber. The format is YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Refrig.description: Object containing refrigerant tracking settings for US companies

UnitsOfMeasure.description:
Unit of measure for tracking refrigerant use.
The possible response values:  • `0`: Pounds and decimals of pounds  • `1`: Pounds and ounces  • `2`: Kilograms and grams
***Note***: To use kilograms and grams as a unit of measure, turn on the *RefrigerantSettingsEU* feature flag.

SubscriberId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the subscriber.

InventoryLocation.description:
Defines whether technicians can take refrigerant from any inventory location or from the locations in the technician's area only.
The possible response values:  • `0`: Only in technician’s area  • `1`: Any location

CalculationMethod.description:
Preferred method of refrigerant leak calculation:  • `0`: Annualized  • `1`: Rolling Average
Check how each calculation method works in [SCU](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/2789703925/Refrigerant+Tracking#RefrigerantTracking).

ChargeThreshold.description: Minimum amount of refrigerant that a system can contain for leak tracking to occur. The charge threshold value is displayed in the specified unit of measure. Check the `UnitsOfMeasure` parameter value.

ComercialRefTriggerRate.description:
Minimum percentage of the total system charge that can be lost before refrigerant tracking to occur. This rate is set for commercial refrigeration appliances.
It applies to asset types with the refrigerant use purpose set to *Commercial Refrigeration*.

IndustrialRefTriggerRate.description:
Minimum percentage of the total system charge that can be lost before refrigerant tracking to occur. This rate is set for industrial refrigeration appliances.
It applies to asset types with the refrigerant use purpose set to *Industrial Refrigeration*.

HVACTriggerRate.description:
Minimum percentage of the total system charge that can be lost before refrigerant tracking to occur. This rate is set for HVAC appliances.
It applies to asset types with the refrigerant use purpose set to *Comfort Cooling (AC)*.

OthersTriggerRate.description:
Minimum percentage of the total system charge that can be lost before refrigerant tracking to occur. This trigger rate is set for appliances that don’t fall under any of the following groups: commercial appliances, industrial appliances, HVAC appliances.
It applies to asset types with the refrigerant use purpose set to *Other Types of Refrigerated Asset*.

Yearly.description:
Minimum threshold for annual leak inspections. The value defines the minimum system charge required to create an annual PM leak inspection work order if a leak has met or exceeded the EPA leak threshold.
Check the `UnitsOfMeasure` parameter value to see the corresponding unit of measure.

Quarterly.description:
Minimum threshold for quarterly leak inspections. The value defines the minimum system charge required to create quarterly PM leak inspection work orders if a leak has met or exceeded the EPA leak threshold.
Check the `UnitsOfMeasure` parameter value to see the corresponding unit of measure.

RunCARBReport.description:
Refrigerant tracking preference that allows subscribers to run the California Air Resources Board report.
The possible response values:  • `true`: The CARB reporting is activated for the subscriber.  • `false`: The CARB reporting is deactivated for the subscriber.
Learn about the CARB reporting in [SCU](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/710148264/California+Air+Resource+Board+CARB+Reporting).

ComplianceAcknowledgmentForAllLeaksRefri.description:
Compliance acknowledgement message that gets triggered for every reported leak or refrigerant use to confirm that a full inspection has been conducted.
The possible response values:  • `true`: The compliance acknowledgement message is enabled in the SC Provider mobile app, Service Automation, and Provider Automation.  • `false`: The compliance acknowledgement message is deactivated.
***Note***: The *RefLeakInspectionAcknowledgementAll* feature flag should be turned on.

DelayedSecondaryVerification.description:
Allows subscribers to enforce a time delay between the initial and the secondary verifications when a leak event takes place.
The possible response values:  • `true`: Time delay is activated by the subscriber. The number of days is specified for each refrigerant type:    * `HVACDelayDays`    * `IndustrialRefrigerationDelayDays`    * `CommercialRefrigerationDelayDays`    * `OtherTypesDelayDays`  • `false`: Time delay is not enabled by the subscriber.
***Note***: The subscriber should have the *RefrigerationTrackingDelayedSecondaryVerification* feature flag enabled.
Read more about this feature in [SCU](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/2789703925/Refrigerant+Tracking#RefrigerantTracking-DelayedSecondaryVerificationDelayedSecondaryVerification).

LeakInspectionNTE.description: Default not-to-exceed (NTE) amount for all PM work orders generated for quarterly and annual follow-up leak inspections.

RefrigerationPriorityName.description: Priority name for Planned Maintenance work orders that are automatically generated for follow-up leak inspections.

EmailNotificationEnable.description:
Allows subscribers to create an email notification that will be sent to the specified recipients when the amount of refrigerant added by a technician meets or exceeds the system total charge.
The possible response values:  • `false`: The email notification is not enabled by the subscriber.  • `true`: The email notification is enabled. The recipients and the message text are specified in the response. When the response value is `true`, check the `EmailNotification` object.

GenerateFollowUpWorkOrder.description:
Defines whether a follow-up work order should be generated when there is an open leak, and the provider wants to close the original work order.
The possible response values:  • `0`: No follow-up work orders should be generated. The work order cannot be closed and invoiced until the leak record is closed. The *Never* option is set by the subscriber for the **Follow-Up Work Order** setting in Refrigerant Tracking Admin.  • `1`: A follow-up work order can be generated for the provider to close the leak record. The *Open Leak* option is set by the subscriber for the **Follow-Up Work Order** setting in Refrigerant Tracking Admin.
***Note***: If the *Open Leak* option is not available for the subscriber, try turning the *RTMultiLeakFollowUp* feature flag on.

Compliance.description:
Shows the region to which the configured refrigerant tracking settings get applied, following the compliance requirements.
The possible response values:  • `US`: Refrigerant tracking compliance for the USA  • `EU`: Refrigerant tracking compliance for the European Union  • `CA`: Refrigerant tracking compliance for Canada

MaxLocCount.description: Maximum number of locations where refrigerant tracking should be recorded. It relates to the `RtLimitedAppliance` parameter.

RtLimitedAppliance.description:
Specifies whether refrigerant tracking should happen across all locations or at those where it’s required.
The possible response values:  • `0`: Across all locations  • `1`: For limited locations only
When the response returns `1`, check the related `MaxLocCount` parameter to learn the max number of locations.

Settings.description: Refrigerant tracking preferences configured for the subscriber.

RefrigerantTrackingProviderId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the provider who is assigned retrofit and retirement work orders, as well as work orders created in the event of adding a refrigerant part use record from the asset details page.

GenerateLeakInspectionOption.description:
Specifies which refrigerant types require PM leak inspection work orders: only ODS (Ozone Depleting Substance) refrigerant types or all refrigerant types.
The possible response values:  • `0`: For all refrigerant types  • `1`: For ODS refrigerant types

OpenLeakNotificationSettings.description: Settings for configuring email alerts about open leaks.

EnableCARBInspections.description:
Shows whether the subscriber has activated PM leak inspections for appliances tracked by CARB (California Air Resources Board).
The possible response values:  • `true`: PM leak inspections are enabled for appliances tracked by CARB. When the parameter is `true`, check the related parameters:    * `DateFormat`    * `CalendarStartDate`    * `CalendarStartDateStr`  • `false`: PM leak inspections are deactivated for appliances tracked by CARB.

DateFormat.description: Date format applied to the `CalendarStartDate` parameter.

CalendarStartDate.description:
Date that becomes a call date for all CARB leak inspection PM work orders. The date format is YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.
Check the `EnableCARBInspections` parameter for more information.

CalendarStartDateStr.description: Date that becomes a call date for all CARB leak inspection PM work orders. The date format is MMM DD, YYYY.

LeakInspectionPMGenerationAdvanceTimefra.description: Number of days to generate PM leak inspection work orders in advance upon identifying a leak. The default value is 7 days.

LeakInspectionCategoryId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the category for PM leak inspection work orders.

SCProviderMessageEnable.description:
Shows whether the subscriber has enabled the compliance acknowledgment message to be displayed for providers in the SC Provider mobile app. Providers receive the message when checking out of PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset.
The possible response values:  • `true`: The acknowledgement message is enabled.  • `false`: The acknowledgement message is deactivated.
Read about the related `SCProviderMessage` parameter to view the message text.
***Note***: The *RefLeakInspectionAcknowledgement* and *RTMultiLeakFlow* feature flags should be turned on.

ServiceAutomationMessageEnable.description:
Shows whether the subscriber has enabled the compliance acknowledgment message to be displayed for subscribers in Service Automation. The message appears when subscribers are entering leak verification information for PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset.
The possible response values:  • `true`: The message is enabled.  • `false`: The message is deactivated.
Check the related `ServiceAutomationMessage` parameter to view the message text.
***Note***: The *RefLeakInspectionAcknowledgement* and *RTMultiLeakFlow* feature flags should be turned on.

ProviderAutomationMessageEnable.description:
Shows whether the subscriber has enabled the compliance acknowledgment message to be displayed for providers in Provider Automation. The message is displayed when providers are entering leak verification information for PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset.
The possible response values:  • `true`: The acknowledgment message is enabled.  • `false`: The acknowledgment message is deactivated.
Check the related `ProviderAutomationMessage` parameter to view the message text.
***Note***: The *RefLeakInspectionAcknowledgement* and *RTMultiLeakFlow* feature flags should be turned on.

SCProviderMessage.description: Compliance acknowledgement message that is displayed for providers in SC Provider upon checking out of PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset. See the parent `SCProviderMessageEnable` parameter for more details.

ServiceAutomationMessage.description: Compliance acknowledgement message that is displayed for subscribers in Service Automation. Subscribers see the message when they are entering leak verification information for PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset.

ProviderAutomationMessage.description: Compliance acknowledgement message that is displayed for providers in Provider Automation. Providers see the message when they are entering leak verification information for PM leak inspection work orders with at least one refrigerated asset.

CertificationExceptionRecipients.description:
Email addresses of people to be notified whenever technicians specify that they don’t have the required trade certification/license while completing a refrigerant or HVAC work order via SC Provider.
***Note***: Available with the *RefCertSCP* feature flag.

CertificationExceptionRecipientEmails.description: Email addresses of people to be notified whenever technicians specify that they don’t have the required trade certification/license while completing a refrigerant or HVAC work order via SC Provider. Available with the RefCertSCP feature flag.

HVACDelayDays.description: Time delay between the initial and the secondary verifications for HVAC assets. Specified in days.

IndustrialRefrigerationDelayDays.description: Time delay between the initial and the secondary verifications for assets of the industrial refrigeration group. Specified in days.

CommercialRefrigerationDelayDays.description: Time delay between the initial and the secondary verifications for assets of the commercial refrigeration type. Specified in days.

OtherTypesDelayDays.description: Time delay between the initial and the secondary verifications for other types of assets that don’t fall under the industrial refrigeration, commercial refrigeration, or HVAC groups. Specified in days.

LocationId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the location (generated by the system).

IsRefrigerantTrackingAvailable.description: Shows whether the refrigerant tracking settings are enabled for the location. Possible response values: `true` and `false`.

UnitsOfMeasure.description:
Unit of measure for tracking refrigerant use. Possible response values:
             • `0`: Pounds and decimals of pounds
             • `1`: Pounds and ounces
             • `2`: Kilograms and grams

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Refrig.description: Object containing information about the leak event.

Id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the leak event. Leak event IDs can be found in the **Refrigerant Leak Events** report in Service Automation.

RepairDate.description: Date when the repair was completed. It cannot be earlier than the work order call date. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`.

InitialDate.description: Date when the first leak verification took place. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`. ***Note:*** The initial verification date cannot be in the future. It should be either a current date or a date in the past.

InitialMethod.description:
Method that was used during the first verification to make sure the leak had been fixed.
Possible values:  • `0`: Unknown  • `1`: Soap Bubble Test  • `2`: Electronic Leak Detection  • `3`: Ultrasonic Leak Detection  • `4`: Pressure Test  • `5`: Vacuum Test  • `6`: Fluorescent Dye Test  • `7`: Infrared Test  • `8`: Near Infrared Test  • `9`: Halon Gas Detection

FollowUpDate.description: Date of the second verification. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`. ***Note:*** The follow-up verification date cannot be earlier than the initial verification date and cannot be in the future. It should be either a current date or a date in the past.

FollowUpMethod.description: Method of the second verification. The list of available verification methods is the same as for the `InitialMethod`.

LeakLocationId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the location where the leak occurred: more specific place within the particular area, for example, *Level Indicator/Alarm*, *Splitting Valve*. Use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/{subscriberId}/leaklocations](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_%7BsubscriberId%7D_leaklocations) method to get the list of available leak locations.

FaultCodeId.description:
Unique numeric identifier of the reason why the problem occurred. Use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/leakRecord/faultCodes](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_leakRecord_faultCodes) method to get available fault codes and their IDs.
Possible values:  • `1`: Accidental Damage  • `2`: Braze or Joint Failure  • `3`: Corrosion  • `4`: Defrost Heater Failure  • `5`: Faulty Part  • `6`: Forklift Damage  • `7`: Gasket Seal Failure  • `8`: Ice Build Up  • `9`: Line Break  • `10`: Manufacture Defect  • `11`: Missing Part  • `12`: Natural Disaster  • `13`: Normal Mechanical Wear  • `14`: Other(Must Explain in Comments)  • `15`: Vandalism  • `16`: Vibration Related  • `17`: Project Related Loss

ActionCodeId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the action that a technician took to fix the leak. Use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/leakRecord/actionCodes](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_leakRecord_actionCodes) method to get available action codes and their IDs.

LeakAreaId.description: Unique numeric identifier of the area where the leak occurred: more general place, for example, *Receiver* or *Compressor*. Use the [GET/refrigeranttracking/leakareas](https://developer.servicechannel.com/swagger/index.html#/RefrigerantTracking/GETv3_refrigeranttracking_leakareas) method to get leak areas and their IDs.

CurrentTrackingNumber.description: Unique numeric identifier of the work order.

CompletedDate.description: Date and time when the leak event was completed. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ`. ***Note:*** The leak event completion date cannot be earlier than the leak event repair date and later than the work order completion date.

Id.description:
Unique numeric identifier of the physical location:
             • `1` = `Indoors`. Applicable to refrigeration or HVAC units installed inside the building, for example, in the restaurant kitchen.
             • `2` = `Outdoors`. Applicable to units positioned outside the building, for example, at the back of the store or on the roof.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.SiteAu.description: Parameters for updating the checklist items.

Id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the checklist item.

Name.description: Checklist item name, for example, *Hand dryer* or *Sink*.

Description.description: Detailed description/instruction for the checklist item.

Score.description:
Shows how the checklist item was rated. The response value depends on the rating system applied:
             • `1`: In the **Pass/Fail** rating system, it stands for the **Fail** answer.
             • `2`: In the **Pass/Fail** rating system, it stands for the **Pass** answer. 
             • `numeric value`: In the **Weighted** rating system, a custom numeric value is assigned to each option: **Good**, **Fair**, and **Fail**.
             • `0–10`: In the **Numeric** rating system, a value from 0 to 10 can be used to rate the item.
             • `0–100`: In the **Percentage** rating system, a value from 0% to 100% can be used to rate the item.

System.description:
Rating system that was applied to the checklist item. Possible values:  • `1`: For the **Pass/Fail** rating system  • `2`: For the **Numeric** rating system  • `3`: For the **Weighted** rating system  • `4`: For the **Percentage** rating system. When this rating system is used, the `Score` value is displayed in percentages.
Learn more about each rating system in [SCU](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/550928611/Building+a+Site+Audit+in+an+Excel+Template).

Date.description: Date and time when the checklist item was inspected and rated. The format is YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssZ.

CheckListItemImpact.description:
Checklist item’s impact on the total audit score. Possible input values:
             • `Veto`: Means that this item has the highest impact on the audit score. When at least one of the veto checklist items is rated as **Fail**, the total score of the audit drops to 1%.
             • `Ignore`: Means that this item is ignored when the audit score is calculated.
             • `Empty value`: Means that this checklist item is counted as a regular item.

PassThreshold.description: Minimum rating value that is sufficient to pass the audit. Can be in numbers or in percentages based on the rating system applied to the checklist item. See the `System` parameter.

Range.description: Range of numbers displayed to the user during the audit, allowing the auditor to rate the item. Permits selecting a score on a 0–10 scale or from 0% to 100%.

The date and time of the check-in. Either indicate in UTC or pass the current time and add the UTC offset.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Workor.description: Check-out request

WorkTypeId.description:
The unique ID of the work type.
            **Possible values:** `1` — Repair, `2` — Travel. Other values are possible when custom types are set up for the subscriber.
            **Default value:** 1.

PrimaryStatus.description:
The status that is set for the WO when checking out.
            Required for the Repair type. Ignored for the Travel and custom types as well when `ActionStatus` = `Cancel`.
            **Default value:** NoStatusChange.

ExtendedStatus.description:
The extended status that is set for the WO when checking out.
            Optional for the Repair type. Ignored for the Travel and custom types, when `ActionStatus` = `Cancel`, and for 'Completed' PrimaryStatus (generated automatically).
            Refrigerant WO with 'Completed' PrimaryStatus — special case by RefrigerationTracking feature.

ActionStatus.description:
The status of the activity.
            **Possible values:** `Complete`, `Cancel`. Both values result in recording a check-out.
            `Complete` means that the technician has finished the activity. `Cancel` means the technician needs to pause the activity, for example, to have a break outside of the location. GPS coordinates are not required.
            **Default value:** Complete.

Resolution.description:
The comment entered when checking out. Usually describes what was done during the recorded time. Ignored for the Travel and custom types as well as when `ActionStatus` = `Cancel`.
            **Default value:** empty.

UserId.description:
The user ID of the technician that is checking out. Use the same `UserId` for one pair of check-in and check-out records.
            **Default value:** ID of the current user.

TechsCount.description:
The number of technicians that are checking out.
            **Default value:** 1.

Latitude.description:
The latitude of the technician’s current position.
            Required for the Repair and Travel type. Not required for custom types, for the Repair and Travel types when the [XML check-in/out permission](/guides/checkin/before-you-start/#xml-check-inout-permission) is enabled, and when `ActionStatus` = `Cancel`.

Longitude.description:
The longitude of the technician’s current position.
            Required for the Repair and Travel type. Not required for custom types, for the Repair and Travel types when the [XML check-in/out permission](/guides/checkin/before-you-start/#xml-check-inout-permission) is enabled, and when `ActionStatus` = `Cancel`.

CheckOutTime.description:
The date and time of the check-out. Either indicate in UTC or pass the current time and add the UTC offset.
            You can pass this value only when the [XML check-in/out permission](/guides/checkin/before-you-start/#xml-check-inout-permission) is enabled.
            **Default value:** current date and time.

            a) The GPS coordinates of the location where the technician performed the most recent action — either check-in or check-out — via the ServiceChannel Provider mobile app.
            b) The phone number of the technician from which they performed the most recent action — either check-in or check-out — using the IVR (Interactive Voice Response) system.
            c) Null value if the work activity was entered manually.

ResolutionCode.description: The most recent status assigned to the work order by the technician.

WorkType.description: The type of activity performed: *Repair* or *Travel*. Other values may be returned if custom types are set up for the subscriber.

HasCheckInInfo.description: Indicates if a check-in was performed for the work activity.

HasCheckListResponse.description: Indicates if the technician answered checklist questions.

TechsCount.description: The number of technicians who performed the work.

CreatedBy.description: The user who created the labor.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Notes..description: Details regarding the resolution status of an action-required note.

IsResolved.description: Indicates whether the action has been resolved. Possible response values: `true` and `false`. Applicable to work order notes that were marked with the **Action Required** flag.

ResolvedDate.description: Date and time when the action was resolved. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssss±hh:mm`, where `±hh:mm` represents the time zone offset from UTC.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Notes..description: Object containing notes for the specified work order ID.

Id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the work order note.

DocumentId.description: UUID of the work order note.

GroupId.description: Numeric identifier of the note group. Some notes can have the same `GroupId`. For example, when a user note is posted along with a WO status change, the `GroupId` will be identical for these two notes. Referring to the `GroupId` helps you easily find the user note associated with the status change. Can be null (for example, for historical notes).

DateCreated.description: Date and time when the note was added to the work order. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sssssss±hh:mm`, where `±hh:mm` represents the time zone offset from UTC.

ScheduledDate.description: Scheduled date of the work order. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`, where `±hh:mm` represents the time zone offset from UTC.

FollowUpDate.description: Follow-up date specified on the note is used to revisit a work order at a later time, for example, to ensure the provider clocked in or updated the work order by the specified date. The format is `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss±hh:mm`, where `±hh:mm` represents the time zone offset from UTC.

ActionRequired.description: Indicates whether the recipient of the note is required to take further action on a work order. Check also the `ActionResolveDetails` parameter to see if the issue has been resolved.

MailedTo.description: Email address(es) to which the note has been sent.

CompanyName.description: Describes who created the note. Works as the `CreatedBy` parameter. ***Note:*** Obsolete parameter.

Attachments.description: Files added along with the note.

IsPinned.description:
Indicates whether the note is pinned to the top of the notes list. Possible response values:  • `true`: The note is pinned, signifying the most important or pressing note right now for this work order. Only one note can be pinned on a single work order.  • `false`: The note isn’t pinned.
Available with the *PinnedNotes* feature flag.

Visibility.description:
Defines which parties can view the note. Visibility also works in Universal Connector, where there are three primary parties: *Subscriber*, *External Subscriber*, and *Provider*. Possible response values:  • `0`: Visible to everyone (subscriber, external subscriber, provider).  • `1`: Visible to the subscriber and the provider. Not visible to the external subscriber.  • `2`: Visible to the subscriber and the external subscriber. Not visible to the provider.  • `3`: Visible to the subscriber only.
Available with the *PrivateProviderNotesAndAttachments* feature flag. For Universal Connector clients, the *PrivateClientNotesAndAttachments* feature should be turned on.

NoteType.description:
Type of the note. Possible response values:
             • `SystemNote`: Notes added automatically by the system.
             • `UsersNote`: Notes posted by users.

IsAttachmentNote.description: Specifies whether the WO note has attachments. Possible values: `true` and `false`.

ActionResolveDetails.description: Applicable to notes that were marked with the **Action Required** flag. Shows whether the issue has been resolved.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Propos.description: Object containing column headers defined in the proposal form.

DataField.description: Database field associated with the column header in the proposal form.

IsDescriptionColumn.description: Points to the description column in the proposal form.

IsMarkUpColumn.description: Shows whether the column accepts the material markup percentage. Available with the *ProposalMaterialMarkup* feature flag.

IsUserReservedColumn.description: Defines whether the column is used for user-specific input.

Name.description: Title of the column header in the proposal form.

IsActive.description: Shows whether the column is active.

SortOrder.description: Order of appearance for column headers in the proposal form.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Propos.description: Object containing cost types broken down into the rows.

Required.description: Defines whether the data entry is mandatory.

HideDetails.description:
Controls whether only the total row is displayed for the proposal cost type in the proposal form.
             • When it returns `true` and the template contains more than one column, only the total row is shown. Other details are hidden.
             • When it returns `false`, cost type details are not hidden.

TotalCost.description: Total cost for all the units of the specified type.

ServiceType.description: Similar to the `FeesType` parameter; specifies the type of service for Excel reporting purposes.

Name.description: Description of the proposal charge type.

IsActive.description: Shows whether the data is active.

Quantity2.description: An auxiliary quantity field used in multi-column templates. Enables extended cost calculations such as: Total = Quantity1 × Quantity2 × UnitCost. If `Quantity2` is missing, a default value of 1 is used.

UnitOfMeasure.description: Unit of measure: each, sq. ft, feet, linear feet, etc.

ExtendedCost.description: Represents the sum of individual row costs. Calculated per row and aggregated into the category total.

Markup.description: Material markup percentage. Available on the proposal behind the *ProposalMaterialMarkup* feature flag.

PriceList.description: Negotiated price list. Learn more in [SCU](https://servicechannel.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SCU/pages/2856484865/Negotiated+Price+Lists).

PartNumber.description: Part number as specified in the negotiated price list.

PartName.description: Part name as specified in the negotiated price list.

FeesType.description: Defines the type of fee applied. Used exclusively in Excel report generation. For example, the "VAT" type will be rendered as "VAT%" in the report.

DoNotApplyMarkup.description: Shows whether the material markup should be applied.

IsDefault.description: Defines which answer is pre-selected by default. Possible values: `true` and `false`.

IsChosen.description: Shows which answer option was chosen upon creating the proposal.

IsActive.description: Shows whether the answer option is active.

ServiceChannel.Services.Messaging.Propos.description: Object containing questions configured in the proposal.

IsRequired.description: Shows whether the question is mandatory.

IsMultipleChoiceAllowed.description: Defines whether multiple answers to the question are allowed.

AnswerType.description:
Indicates how the response is structured and displayed in the proposal form. Possible values:
             • `SINGLE_QUESTION`
             • `DROPDOWN`

Name.description: Question associated with the proposal. Check the `Options` parameter to view available answers to the question.

IsActive.description: Shows whether the question is active.

IsLocked.description:
Controls the visibility of the category section, for example, *Materials*, *Installation Labor*, in the proposal form. Possible values: 
             • `true`: The section (category) is hidden from the user interface.
             • `false`: The section (category) is visible in the user interface.

DefaultHideDetails.description:
Determines whether the category displays a standard template or extended rows. Possible values:
             • `true`: Shows the default template without additional rows.
             • `false`: Displays extended rows based on the template configuration.

IsActive.description: Shows whether the category is active.

SortOrder.description: Predefined order of appearance for a category.

Id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the proposal category.

Name.description: Type of proposal categories, for example, *Materials*, *Installation Labor*, *Non-Installation Expenses*, etc.

TotalCost.description: Subtotal for the specific cost type, for example, materials.
